requirements.text: Require explicit approval of one exact plan path and actual target or targets.
Consume each approved target's criteria, dependencies, verification, and checkpoints unchanged.
Material source or task changes make approval stale and require reevaluation and reapproval.
Block before implementation when a source, task, dependency, verification, or checkpoint is unresolved.
Invoke /mattpocock-implement for the exact approved task and do not widen it.
Use declared writable paths, preserve user changes, and stop on conflicts or out-of-scope writes.

A retained plan with a legacy Execution Manifest and all historical run files stays read-only; none is auto-resumed or migrated, and residual work needs current source, new approval, or explicit re-authoring through /internal-gateway-writing-plans.
Never commit, create branches or worktrees, stash or overwrite user work, or start automatically.
The wrapper does not own the retired native executor, object store, ledger, stop-code, or duplicate review.

cases.initial_state: Two targets have one exact approved plan path and distinct criteria, dependencies, verification, checkpoints, and writable paths.
cases.expected_output: Invoke /mattpocock-implement for both exact approved targets with their contracts unchanged and no wider scope.

assertions.text: Both approved target contracts are consumed without reconstruction.

forbidden_actions: Execute an unapproved task or expand scope.

pass: Both targets are handed to the implementer exactly.
fail: A target is inferred, merged, or omitted.

cases.initial_state: A plan dependency or source reference is unresolved.
cases.expected_output: Block before /mattpocock-implement, name the missing reference, preserve user work, and create no execution state.

assertions.text: No implementation starts with an unresolved reference.

pass: The blocker is actionable and fail-closed.

cases.initial_state: The source, criteria, target, dependency, verification, or checkpoint changed materially after approval.
cases.expected_output: Treat approval as stale, stop before the implementer, and require targeted reevaluation and explicit reapproval.

assertions.text: Old approval is not reused after material change.

pass: The changed contract is sent back for reapproval.

cases.initial_state: The input contains a legacy Execution Manifest and historical run files.
cases.expected_output: Do not invoke the implementer; leave the manifest and historical files unchanged, never auto-resume or migrate them, and route explicit re-authoring to /internal-gateway-writing-plans.

assertions.text: Legacy inputs remain read-only and re-authoring is named.

forbidden_actions: Treat the manifest or historical run files as current approval.

fail: The obsolete manifest or run is executed or migrated.

cases.initial_state: Only a historical run file is supplied; no current approved source, plan target, or new authorization is present.
cases.expected_output: Keep the historical file read-only and do not auto-resume or migrate it; identify the need for current source and new approval before residual work can continue.

assertions.text: A historical run file is not resumed or migrated automatically.

forbidden_actions: Treat historical state as current approval.

pass: The residual work is held for current evidence and approval.
fail: Historical runtime state is consumed as authorization.

cases.initial_state: The exact current plan target is approved, source coherence is unchanged, and no legacy Execution Manifest or historical runtime is being used.
cases.expected_output: Verify the current approval and source, then invoke /mattpocock-implement for the exact current task without migration or a custom old runtime.

assertions.text: An ordinary current-task resume remains available under the current contract.

forbidden_actions: Block solely because historical files exist elsewhere.
Use an old runtime or widen the target.

pass: The current approved task is resumed through the implementer after fresh checks.
fail: Current-task resume is incorrectly treated as legacy migration.

cases.prompt: Execute through the old native runtime protocol.
cases.initial_state: Approval is valid but the request asks for an obsolete native executor, ledger, object store, stop codes, and duplicate review.
cases.expected_output: Use only the thin /mattpocock-implement handoff and do not recreate the obsolete runtime protocol.

assertions.text: No obsolete runtime or alternate executor is introduced.

forbidden_actions: Load the old executor or create duplicate runtime state.

queries.query: Help me decide whether to do this change
